items.title: Leave to file a late defendant's claim
items.says: After the 20 days, a defendant's claim may be issued before trial or default judgment only with the court's leave.

source.expect: before trial or default judgment, with leave of the court

items.title: Serving the defendant's claim
items.says: The defendant serves the defendant's claim on every person it is made against, the same way and within the same six months as a plaintiff's claim.

source.expect: shall be served by the defendant on every person against whom it is made

items.title: Defence to a defendant's claim within 20 days
items.says: A party disputing a defendant's claim, or a third party disputing the plaintiff's claim, serves and files a defence (Form 9A) within 20 days after service of the defendant's claim.

source.expect: within 20 days after service of the defendant's claim

items.title: Defendant's claim tried with the main case
items.says: A defendant's claim is tried together with the main case unless the court orders otherwise. The court may order separate trials if it would unduly complicate or delay the trial or cause undue prejudice.

source.expect: unduly complicate or delay the trial

items.title: Third party may contest the plaintiff's claim
items.says: A third party said to be liable for the plaintiff's claim may challenge the defendant's liability to the plaintiff at trial, but only if the third party filed a defence.

source.expect: may at the trial contest the defendant's liability to the plaintiff

items.title: Default on a defendant's claim
items.says: If a party to a defendant's claim is noted in default, judgment against them may be obtained only at trial or on motion.

source.expect: only at trial or on motion

items.title: Noting the defendant in default
items.says: If a defendant does not file a defence in time, the clerk may note them in default when the plaintiff files a request (Form 9B) and proof of service. A person under disability may be noted in default only with leave.

source.expect: the clerk may note the defendant in default

items.title: Form 11A: Affidavit for jurisdiction
items.says: If all defendants were served outside the court's territorial division, the clerk will not note default until an affidavit for jurisdiction (Form 11A) or evidence before a judge shows the case was properly brought there.

source.expect: affidavit for jurisdiction (Form 11A)

items.title: Default judgment for a debt (Form 11B)
items.says: Once a defendant is noted in default, the clerk may sign default judgment (Form 11B) for the part of the claim that is a debt or fixed (liquidated) amount of money, including interest if claimed. The clerk serves it on all parties named in the claim.

source.expect: debt or liquidated demand in money

items.title: Assessment of damages for amounts not fixed
items.says: If all defendants are noted in default, the plaintiff may get judgment for any non-fixed amount by a motion in writing for an assessment of damages (Form 15A) or by requesting an assessment hearing (Form 9B).

source.expect: motion in writing for an assessment of damages

items.title: At an assessment, only the amount is proved
items.says: On an assessment motion or hearing, the plaintiff does not have to prove liability against a defendant noted in default, but must prove the amount of the claim.

source.expect: is not required to prove liability

items.title: Assessment hearing
items.says: If a judge finds the affidavit inadequate, or the plaintiff asks for one, the clerk sets an assessment hearing, which proceeds like a trial.

source.expect: shall proceed as a trial in accordance with rule 17

items.title: Assessment when another defendant defended
items.says: If one or more defendants filed a defence, the assessment against a defendant in default goes through the settlement conference and, if needed, trial.

source.expect: shall proceed to a settlement conference under rule 13

items.title: What noting in default means
items.says: A defendant noted in default cannot file a defence or take other steps, except a motion to set aside, without leave or the plaintiff's consent, and is not entitled to notice of most later steps.

source.expect: shall not file a defence or take any other step

items.title: Motion to set aside noting in default or default judgment
items.says: The court may set aside a noting in default or default judgment, and enforcement steps, on just terms, if the party has a meritorious defence and a reasonable explanation for the default, and moved as soon as reasonably possible.

source.expect: meritorious defence and a reasonable explanation for the default

items.title: Clerk dismisses a case after two years
items.says: Unless the court orders otherwise, the clerk dismisses a case for delay if, by the second anniversary of its start, it has not been decided and the plaintiff has not taken a step to get default judgment by assessment or asked for a trial date.

source.expect: by the second anniversary of the commencement of the action

items.title: When the two-year dismissal does not apply
items.says: The automatic dismissal does not apply if an accepted offer was filed, the defence admits liability and proposes payment terms, or the plaintiff is under disability.

source.expect: an offer to settle the action has been accepted and filed

items.title: Effect on a defendant's claim
items.says: If the main case is dismissed for delay, a defendant's claim is treated as dismissed 60 days after the order is served, unless the court orders otherwise in that time.

source.expect: deemed to be dismissed 60 days after the order

items.title: Clerk's order on consent (Form 11.2A)
items.says: If all parties (including any party being added, deleted or substituted) sign a request for clerk's order on consent (Form 11.2A) stating that each received a copy and that no affected party is under disability, the clerk makes an order for certain things: amending a claim or defence or changing parties less than 30 days before the original trial date, setting aside a noting in default or default judgment, restoring a case dismissed for delay, noting payment in full, or dismissing a case.

source.expect: request for clerk's order on consent (Form 11.2A)

review.problem: It drops a condition of the rule: the signed request must also state that each party received a copy and that no affected party is under disability, so all parties signing is not enough by itself.

items.title: If the clerk refuses the consent order
items.says: If the clerk refuses, the clerk serves the request with reasons on all parties.

source.expect: with reasons for the refusal

items.title: Discontinuing a claim (Form 11.3A)
items.says: A plaintiff may discontinue a claim against a defendant who has not filed a defence by serving a notice of discontinued claim (Form 11.3A) on all served defendants and filing it with proof of service. Leave is needed if a person under disability is involved.

source.expect: notice of discontinued claim (Form 11.3A)

items.title: Discontinuance does not end the right to sue again
items.says: Discontinuing a claim is not a defence to a later case on the same matter, unless an order granting leave to discontinue says otherwise.

source.expect: is not a defence to a subsequent action

items.title: Withdrawing a claim after the settlement conference
items.says: After a settlement conference, a claim against a party not in default can be withdrawn only with that party's written consent or the court's leave.

source.expect: shall not be withdrawn or discontinued

items.title: Amending a claim or defence
items.says: A claim or defence may be amended by filing a version marked "Amended" with additions underlined and changes identified, attaching the documents it relies on. It is served on all parties, including those in default.

source.expect: Any additions shall be underlined

items.title: Amend at least 30 days before trial
items.says: An amended claim or defence must be filed and served at least 30 days before the originally scheduled trial date, unless the court allows less time or a clerk's consent order permits it.

source.expect: at least 30 days before the originally scheduled trial date

items.title: Motion to strike out or amend a document
items.says: The court may strike out or amend all or part of a document that discloses no reasonable cause of action or defence, may delay or prevent a fair trial, or is inflammatory, a waste of time, a nuisance or an abuse of process. It may then stay or dismiss the case or strike the defence and grant judgment.

source.expect: discloses no reasonable cause of action or defence

items.title: Court may dismiss an abusive claim on its own
items.says: The court may, on its own, stay or dismiss a case that on its face is inflammatory, a waste of time, a nuisance or an abuse of process. The plaintiff is first sent notice and may file a written response of no more than four pages within 20 days.

source.expect: no more than four pages in length

items.title: Settlement conference in every defended case
items.says: A settlement conference must be held in every defended case. The clerk sets it and serves notice with a list of proposed witnesses form (Form 13A). It does not happen if the defence admits all of the claim and proposes payment terms.

source.expect: shall be held in every defended action

items.title: Settlement conference within 90 days
items.says: The settlement conference is to be held within 90 days after the first defence is filed.

source.expect: within 90 days after the first defence is filed

items.title: Disclosure 14 days before the settlement conference
items.says: At least 14 days before the settlement conference, each party must serve and file a copy of every document to be relied on at trial (including expert reports) not already attached to the claim or defence, and a list of proposed witnesses and others with knowledge (Form 13A).

source.expect: At least 14 days before the date of the settlement conference

items.title: Who must take part
items.says: Each party and their representative must take part unless the court orders otherwise. A party who needs someone else's approval to settle must arrange ready telephone access to that person throughout.

source.expect: ready telephone access

items.title: Missing the settlement conference
items.says: If a party misses the conference, the court may impose costs or other sanctions and order another conference. If a defendant misses two, the court may strike the defence and let the plaintiff prove the claim. Costs may also be ordered for being so unprepared as to frustrate the conference.

source.expect: strike out the defence and dismiss the defendant's claim

items.title: Purposes of the settlement conference
items.says: The conference aims to resolve or narrow the issues, speed things up, encourage settlement, help the parties prepare for trial, and give full disclosure of facts and evidence. The parties discuss the issues openly and frankly.

source.expect: to resolve or narrow the issues in the action

items.title: What is said at the conference stays private
items.says: Unless the parties consent (Form 13B) or the rules provide otherwise, what is discussed at the settlement conference is not disclosed to others until the case is over.

source.expect: shall not be disclosed to others until after the action has been disposed of

items.title: Judge's recommendations
items.says: The judge may make recommendations about simplifying issues, dropping claims or defences that appear unsupported, and admitting facts or documents without further proof.

source.expect: the elimination of claims or defences that appear to be unsupported

items.title: Orders a judge may make at the conference
items.says: The judge may make any order about the conduct of the case, such as adding or deleting parties, consolidating cases, staying or dismissing the case with written reasons, amending or striking out a claim or defence, ordering production of documents, changing the place of trial, or ordering costs.

source.expect: directing production of documents

items.title: Final judgment at the settlement conference by consent
items.says: If the amount in dispute is under the appeal limit and all parties sign a consent (Form 13B), the judge may give final judgment at the conference if a mediated settlement is not reached.

source.expect: final determination of the matter at the settlement conference

items.title: Settlement conference memorandum
items.says: At the end of the settlement conference, the court prepares a memorandum summarizing its recommendations, the issues still in dispute, what the parties agreed, relevant evidence matters and scheduling. It is filed with the clerk, who gives a copy to the trial judge.

source.expect: prepare a memorandum summarizing

review.problem: That the conference judge does not preside at trial is r. 13.08, not r. 13.06.

items.title: Cost of a settlement conference
items.says: Costs of a settlement conference, other than disbursements, may not be more than $100 unless the court finds special circumstances.

source.expect: shall not exceed $100 unless the court orders otherwise

items.title: Request a trial date within 30 days
items.says: The clerk gives notice that if the case is not resolved within 30 days after the settlement conference, a party must request a trial date and pay the fee.

source.expect: within 30 days after the settlement conference

items.title: Offer to settle (Form 14A)
items.says: An offer to settle, an acceptance and a notice of withdrawal must be in writing. An offer may be made in Form 14A, an acceptance in Form 14B and a withdrawal in Form 14C.

source.expect: An offer to settle may be in Form 14A

review.problem: Rule 14.01.1 says offers, acceptances and withdrawals must be in writing and names the forms; that an offer may be made at any time is r. 14.02(1), not the cited rule.

items.title: Offer at least seven days before trial for costs consequences
items.says: The special costs consequences apply only if the offer is served at least seven days before the trial starts.

source.expect: at least seven days before the trial commences

items.title: Withdrawing or expiry of an offer
items.says: An offer may be withdrawn any time before acceptance by serving a notice of withdrawal on the party it was made to. An offer with an end date is treated as withdrawn the day after that date if not accepted, and no offer can be accepted after the court decides the claim.

source.expect: may be withdrawn at any time before it is accepted

review.problem: Rule 14.03 does not name Form 14C; the form number comes from r. 14.01.1(2).

items.title: Offers are kept from the trial judge
items.says: If an offer is not accepted, nothing about it or the negotiations is told to the trial judge until liability and relief (other than costs) are decided.

source.expect: no communication about it or any related negotiations

items.title: Accepting an offer (Form 14B)
items.says: An offer is accepted by serving an acceptance on the party who made it, before the offer is withdrawn or the court decides the claim. If the accepted offer does not deal with costs, the plaintiff gets disbursements assessed up to the date set by the rule.

source.expect: serving an acceptance of an offer to settle on the party who made it

review.problem: Rule 14.05 does not name Form 14B or terms of settlement (Form 14D); those come from r. 14.01.1.

items.title: Form 14D: Terms of settlement
items.says: The terms of an accepted offer to settle may be set out in terms of settlement (Form 14D).

source.expect: terms of settlement (Form 14D)

items.title: Offer requiring payment into court
items.says: A plaintiff's offer may require the defendant to pay the money into court; the defendant then accepts only by paying in and telling the plaintiff. A plaintiff may also accept a defendant's money offer on condition it is paid into court.

source.expect: the defendant may accept the offer only by paying the money into court

items.title: When a party breaks an accepted offer
items.says: If a party does not comply with an accepted offer, the other party may move for judgment in the terms of the offer or continue the case as if there had been no offer.

source.expect: judgment in the terms of the accepted offer

items.title: Costs when a plaintiff's offer is refused
items.says: If the plaintiff's offer was not accepted, the plaintiff gets a judgment as good as or better than the offer, the offer was made at least seven days before trial and did not expire or get withdrawn, the court may award up to twice the costs of the action, not counting disbursements.

source.expect: an amount not exceeding twice the costs of the action

items.title: Costs when a defendant's offer is refused
items.says: If the defendant's offer was not accepted and the plaintiff's judgment is as good as or less favourable than the offer, under the same timing conditions, the court may award the defendant up to twice the costs awardable to a successful party from the date the offer was served.

source.expect: from the date the offer was served

items.title: Extra compensation for a self-represented party
items.says: If an amount is awarded under the offer rules to a self-represented party, the court may also award up to $1,500 for inconvenience and expense.

source.expect: an amount not exceeding $1,500

items.title: Making a motion (Form 15A)
items.says: A motion is a request for a court order during the case. It is made by a notice of motion and supporting affidavit (Form 15A). The moving party first gets a hearing date from the clerk.

source.expect: notice of motion and supporting affidavit (Form 15A)

items.title: Serve a motion seven days before the hearing
items.says: The notice of motion and affidavit are served on every party who filed a claim and any defendant not in default at least seven days before the hearing, and filed with proof of service at least three days before.

source.expect: at least seven days before the hearing date

items.title: Responding affidavit two days before the hearing
items.says: A party responding to a motion with an affidavit (Form 15B) serves it on every party who has filed a claim or defence and files it, with proof of service, at least two days before the hearing.

source.expect: at least two days before the hearing date

review.problem: The moving party's supplementary affidavit is in r. 15.01(5), not the cited r. 15.01(4).

items.title: Motions after judgment
items.says: A motion made after judgment has been signed must be served on all parties, including those noted in default.

source.expect: including those who have been noted in default

items.title: How a motion is heard
items.says: A motion is heard with the parties attending by a method under rule 1.07, or in writing if the rules provide for it or the judge finds it fair and reasonable.

source.expect: fair and reasonable for the motion to be in writing

items.title: Motion without notice
items.says: A motion may be made without notice if its nature or circumstances make notice unnecessary or not reasonably possible. The party who gets the order must serve it, with the motion materials, on affected parties within five days.

source.expect: make notice unnecessary or not reasonably possible

items.title: Setting aside an order made without notice
items.says: A party affected by an order made without notice may move to set it aside or vary it within 30 days after being served with it.

source.expect: within 30 days after being served with the order

items.title: Stopping repeated meritless motions
items.says: If a party has tried to delay or abuse the process by making many motions without merit, the court may bar further motions without leave.

source.expect: making numerous motions without merit

items.title: Adjourning or withdrawing a motion
items.says: A motion is not adjourned at a party's request before the hearing date unless all parties' written consent is filed with the request, unless the court orders otherwise.

source.expect: unless the written consent of all parties is filed

review.problem: The withdrawal limit (all parties' written consent or leave) is r. 15.06, not r. 15.05, which deals only with adjournment.

items.title: Costs of a motion
items.says: Costs of a motion, other than disbursements, may not be more than $100 unless the court finds special circumstances.

source.expect: shall not exceed $100 unless the court orders otherwise

items.title: Fixing the trial date
items.says: After a settlement conference, once a party files a request to clerk (Form 9B) to fix a trial date and pays the fee, the clerk sets the date and serves a notice of trial by mail or email.

source.expect: to fix a date for trial and has paid the required fee

items.title: Trial management conference
items.says: After a request to fix a trial date is filed, the court may on its own direct that a trial management conference be held before a judge. The parties and their representatives take part unless the court directs otherwise, the clerk sets and serves notice of it, and the court may impose costs or other sanctions on a party who does not attend or who is so unprepared as to frustrate it.

source.expect: direct that a trial management conference be held before a judge

review.problem: The purposes, the $100 costs limit and the bar on the conference judge presiding at trial are in rr. 16.1.02, 16.1.07 and 16.1.06, not r. 16.1.01.

items.title: Serve written evidence 30 days before trial
items.says: A document, written statement, or audio or visual record served at least 30 days before the trial date on all parties who were served with the notice of trial is received in evidence, unless the trial judge orders otherwise.

source.expect: at least 30 days before the trial date

review.problem: The list of statements and documents (witness statements, expert reports, medical records, receipts, bills, repair estimates) is in r. 18.02(2); r. 18.02(1) also limits service to parties who were served with the notice of trial, not all parties.

items.title: Details of the witness or author
items.says: A party serving such a statement or document must include the name, phone number and address for service of the witness or author and, for an expert, a summary of qualifications. The other side may summon that person to cross-examine.

source.expect: a summary of his or her qualifications

items.title: Summons to witness (Form 18A)
items.says: A party who needs a person in Ontario as a witness may serve a summons to witness (Form 18A), which may also require them to bring documents or things.

source.expect: summons to witness (Form 18A)

items.title: Serve a summons 10 days before trial
items.says: A summons to witness must be served personally at least 10 days before the trial date, with attendance money paid or offered to the witness at that time.

source.expect: at least 10 days before the trial date

items.title: Interpreter for a summoned witness
items.says: A party who summons a witness who needs an interpreter must arrange a qualified interpreter (except English-French interpretation provided by the Ministry). Otherwise other parties may ask for an adjournment with costs.

source.expect: shall arrange for a qualified interpreter

items.title: Warrant for a witness who does not attend (Form 18B)
items.says: If a summoned witness with material evidence fails to attend or stay, the trial judge may issue a warrant (Form 18B) for police to bring the witness to court. An identification form (Form 20K) may be filed to help.

source.expect: by warrant (Form 18B)

items.title: Proving an undefended case by affidavit
items.says: At the trial of an undefended case, the plaintiff's case may be proved by affidavit unless the judge orders otherwise.

source.expect: the plaintiff's case may be proved by affidavit

items.title: Adjourning a trial
items.says: A trial may be adjourned only by court order, on just terms, which may include one party paying the other for inconvenience and expense.

source.expect: A trial may be adjourned only by order of the court

items.title: Judge may inspect property
items.says: The trial judge may inspect real or personal property in question, with the parties or their representatives present.

source.expect: inspect any real or personal property

items.title: When a party misses the trial
items.says: If a party does not attend, the judge may go ahead without them, strike out the absent defendant's defence and let the plaintiff prove the claim, dismiss the absent plaintiff's case, or make another just order. If everyone is absent, the case may be struck off the list. The attending party need only prove the amount, not liability.

source.expect: proceed with the trial in the party's absence

items.title: Setting aside a judgment after missing trial
items.says: The court may set aside or vary a judgment against a party who missed the trial, but only if they move within 30 days after becoming aware of the judgment, or the court extends that time for special circumstances.

source.expect: within 30 days after becoming aware of the judgment

items.title: Motion for a new trial
items.says: A party may move for a new trial within 30 days after a final order, and must serve and file proof that a transcript of the reasons (and other relevant parts) was requested.

source.expect: within 30 days after a final order is made

items.title: Grounds for a new trial
items.says: The court may grant a new trial or give the judgment that ought to have been given at trial only if there was a purely arithmetical error in the damages, or relevant evidence was not available at trial and could not reasonably have been expected to be available.

source.expect: purely arithmetical error

items.title: Paying a judgment by instalments
items.says: The court may order the times and proportions in which money owed under its order is paid.

source.expect: may order the times and the proportions

items.title: 15% limit on costs
items.says: Costs in Small Claims Court, other than disbursements, may not exceed 15% of the amount claimed or the value of property sought, unless the court finds it necessary to penalize unreasonable behaviour.

source.expect: shall not exceed 15 per cent of the amount claimed

items.title: Disbursements for the successful party
items.says: A successful party is entitled to reasonable disbursements (such as service, preparing the claim or defence, filing fees, travel, photocopying and expert reports) paid by the unsuccessful party, unless the court orders otherwise. Service is capped at $60 per person and preparing a claim or defence at $200.

source.expect: shall not exceed $200

items.title: Service disbursement limit
items.says: Disbursements for serving a document may not exceed $60 for each person served unless special circumstances justify more.

source.expect: shall not exceed $60 for each person served

items.title: Representation fee
items.says: If a successful party has a lawyer, student-at-law or paralegal, the court may award a reasonable representation fee at trial or an assessment hearing.

source.expect: a reasonable representation fee

items.title: Compensation for a self-represented winner
items.says: The court may order the unsuccessful party to pay a successful self-represented party up to $500 for inconvenience and expense.

source.expect: an amount not exceeding $500

items.title: Penalty for unreasonable conduct
items.says: If a party or representative unduly complicated or prolonged the case or acted unreasonably, the court may order them to pay a penalty to another party, as section 29 of the Courts of Justice Act provides.

source.expect: has unduly complicated or prolonged an action

items.title: Appeal to the Divisional Court
items.says: A final order of the Small Claims Court can be appealed to the Divisional Court if it is for more than the set amount of money (not counting costs), or for personal property worth more than that amount.

source.expect: An appeal lies to the Divisional Court from a final order

items.title: The $5,000 appeal limit
items.says: The amount a final order must exceed to be appealed is $5,000.

source.expect: the prescribed amount is $5,000

items.title: Leave needed to appeal a consent order or costs only
items.says: No appeal lies without leave from an order made with the parties' consent, or where the appeal is only about discretionary costs.

source.expect: from an order made with the consent of the parties

items.title: Notice of appeal within 30 days
items.says: An appeal to the Divisional Court starts by serving a notice of appeal (Form 61A.3) with the appellant's certificate respecting evidence within 30 days after the order is made, unless a statute or the rules provide otherwise, on every party whose interest may be affected and anyone entitled by statute to be heard.

source.expect: within 30 days after the making of the order appealed from

review.problem: Filing the notice of appeal within 10 days after service is in r. 61.04(4), not the cited r. 61.04(1).

items.title: Appellant's certificate respecting evidence (Form 61C)
items.says: With the notice of appeal, the appellant serves and files a certificate (Form 61C) listing only the parts of the evidence needed for the appeal.

source.expect: appellant's certificate respecting evidence (Form 61C)

items.title: Perfecting the appeal
items.says: The appellant perfects the appeal within 30 days after filing the notice of appeal if no transcript is needed, or within 60 days after notice that the transcript is ready.

source.expect: within thirty days after filing the notice of appeal

items.title: Appeal pauses payment
items.says: Delivering a notice of appeal stays (pauses) the part of the order requiring payment of money until the appeal is decided, except support orders.

source.expect: stays, until the disposition of the appeal

items.title: Ways to enforce a money judgment
items.says: An order for money may be enforced by a writ of seizure and sale of personal property (Form 20C), a writ of seizure and sale of land (Form 20D), garnishment, and a further order as to payment after an examination.

source.expect: may be enforced by

items.title: Form 20P: Affidavit for enforcement request
items.says: A creditor's request for a certificate of judgment is supported by an affidavit for enforcement request (Form 20P) stating the amount still owing.

source.expect: affidavit for enforcement request (Form 20P)

review.problem: Rule 20.04(1) uses Form 20P only for a request for a certificate of judgment; it does not say that most enforcement requests use it.

items.title: Staying enforcement or changing payments
items.says: The court may stay enforcement for a time on just terms, and may change the times and amounts of payments if the debtor's circumstances have changed.

source.expect: if it is satisfied that the debtor's circumstances have changed

items.title: Enforcement paused during a payment order
items.says: While an order for periodic payments is in force, the creditor named in it may not take enforcement steps except issuing a writ of seizure and sale of land and filing it with the sheriff.

source.expect: except issuing a writ of seizure and sale of land

items.title: Default under a periodic payment order
items.says: If the debtor misses payments, the creditor may serve a notice of default of payment (Form 20L) and file it with an affidavit of default (Form 20M). The payment order ends 15 days after service unless the creditor files a consent (Form 13B) waiving the default.

source.expect: 15 days after the creditor serves the debtor

items.title: Certificate of judgment (Form 20A)
items.says: If payment is not made, the clerk will issue a certificate of judgment (Form 20A) to another court location chosen by the creditor, so the judgment can be enforced there.

source.expect: issue a certificate of judgment (Form 20A)

items.title: Writ of delivery (Form 20B)
items.says: An order to deliver personal property may be enforced by a writ of delivery (Form 20B) issued to a bailiff. If the property cannot be found, the court may order the bailiff to seize other property of the person.

source.expect: writ of delivery (Form 20B)

items.title: Writ of seizure and sale of personal property (Form 20C)
items.says: On request with Form 20P, the clerk issues a writ of seizure and sale of personal property (Form 20C) to a bailiff, who enforces it for the amount owing, interest and the bailiff's fees. Enforcement starts when the creditor files a direction to enforce (Form 20O).

source.expect: writ of seizure and sale of personal property (Form 20C)

items.title: Form 20O: Direction to enforce
items.says: The creditor asks the bailiff to enforce a writ of seizure and sale of personal property by filing a direction to enforce (Form 20O).

source.expect: (Form 20O) with the bailiff

items.title: Leave needed after six years
items.says: If more than six years have passed since the order, a writ of seizure and sale of personal property may be issued only with the court's leave. A leave order lapses if the writ is not issued within one year, and a new motion is then needed.

source.expect: If more than six years have passed since the order was made

review.problem: Rule 20.06(1.1) covers only a writ of seizure and sale of personal property; leave for a notice of garnishment is r. 20.08(2.1).

items.title: Writs last six years and can be renewed
items.says: A writ of seizure and sale expires six years after it is issued, and may be renewed before it expires by filing a request to renew (Form 20N).

source.expect: expires on the sixth anniversary of the date of its issue

items.title: Notice before a bailiff sells property
items.says: Seized property may not be sold unless notice of the time and place is mailed to the creditor and debtor at least 10 days before the sale and advertised to the public. The debtor may ask for an inventory of what was seized.

source.expect: at least 10 days before the sale

items.title: Property exempt from seizure
items.says: An individual debtor may claim certain property as exempt from seizure, such as necessary clothing, household furnishings and tools of the trade up to set values, and one motor vehicle up to a set value.

source.expect: exempt from forced seizure or sale

items.title: Writ of seizure and sale of land (Form 20D)
items.says: If a money order is unpaid, the clerk issues a writ of seizure and sale of land (Form 20D) to the sheriff the creditor names. Once issued, the Rules of Civil Procedure govern it as if issued under rule 60.07.

source.expect: writ of seizure and sale of land (Form 20D)

items.title: Land writ follows the civil rules
items.says: An issued writ of seizure and sale of land is governed by the Rules of Civil Procedure, except that it lasts six years and may be renewed with Form 20N filed with the sheriff.

source.expect: as if the writ were a writ of seizure and sale issued under rule 60.07

items.title: Garnishment
items.says: A creditor may enforce a money order by garnishing debts that others owe the debtor, such as wages or bank accounts. For a jointly owned debt, one-half may be garnished unless the court orders otherwise.

source.expect: by garnishment of debts payable to the debtor

items.title: Getting a notice of garnishment (Form 20E)
items.says: The creditor files Form 20P naming one debtor and one garnishee (and a certificate of judgment if the order was made elsewhere) with the clerk where the debtor lives or does business. The clerk issues a notice of garnishment (Form 20E).

source.expect: in which the debtor resides or carries on business

items.title: Serving the garnishment
items.says: The creditor serves the notice of garnishment with a garnishee's statement form (Form 20F) on the garnishee, and serves it with Form 20P on the debtor within five days after serving the garnishee. For a bank, service is at the branch where the debt is payable.

source.expect: within five days of serving it on the garnishee

items.title: Garnishment lasts six years (Form 20E.1)
items.says: A notice of garnishment stays in force for six years and may be renewed for six more years each time by filing a notice of renewal of garnishment (Form 20E.1) with Form 20P before it expires.

source.expect: remains in force for six years from the date of its issue

items.title: Garnishee must pay the clerk
items.says: The garnishee must pay the clerk what it owes the debtor, up to the amount in the notice, within 10 days after being served or after the debt becomes payable, whichever is later. Paying someone else does not end its liability.

source.expect: within 10 days after service of the notice on the garnishee

items.title: 80% of wages are protected
items.says: 80% of a person's wages are exempt from seizure or garnishment, or 50% when an order for support or maintenance is being enforced. Amounts the employer must deduct by law are not counted as wages.

source.expect: wages are exempt from seizure or garnishment

review.problem: Section 7 of the Wages Act does not say a garnishee pays into court only the non-exempt part; that limit is in Small Claims rule 20.08(9) (s. 7(6) only lets an employer pay the non-exempt part into court when a motion to change the exemption is brought).

items.title: Changing the wage exemption
items.says: A debtor may ask a judge to increase the exempt part of wages, and a creditor may ask to decrease it, if the judge finds it just considering the person's financial circumstances and other relevant matters.

source.expect: be increased, if the judge is satisfied that it is just

items.title: Garnishee's statement (Form 20F)
items.says: A garnishee that disputes the garnishment or pays less than the amount in the notice (for example because of a co-owner) must file a garnishee's statement (Form 20F) within 10 days after service and serve it on the creditor and debtor.

source.expect: file with the court a statement (Form 20F)

items.title: Notice to co-owner of debt (Form 20G)
items.says: A creditor served with a garnishee's statement must send any co-owner of the debt a notice to co-owner (Form 20G). A co-owner who wants to dispute must request a garnishment hearing within 30 days after the notice is sent.

source.expect: requests a garnishment hearing within 30 days after the notice is sent

items.title: Garnishment hearing (Form 20Q)
items.says: The creditor, debtor, garnishee, co-owner or another interested person may ask the clerk to schedule a garnishment hearing, and serves a notice of garnishment hearing (Form 20Q). The court may decide everyone's rights and vary or suspend payments.

source.expect: vary or suspend periodic payments

items.title: Garnishee that neither pays nor responds
items.says: If the garnishee neither pays the clerk nor files a garnishee's statement, the creditor is entitled to an order against the garnishee for the amount in the notice, unless the court orders otherwise.

source.expect: the creditor is entitled to an order against the garnishee

items.title: When garnished money is paid out
items.says: Once proof of service on the debtor is filed, the clerk pays the first garnishment payment out 30 days after receiving it and later payments as received, unless a hearing, set-aside motion or consent request is pending. Payments are shared equally among creditors with garnishments.

source.expect: 30 days after the date it is received

items.title: Ending a garnishment (Form 20R)
items.says: Once the amount owing is paid, the creditor must immediately serve a notice of termination of garnishment (Form 20R) on the garnishee and the clerk.

source.expect: notice of termination of garnishment (Form 20R)

items.title: Consolidation order
items.says: A debtor with two or more unpaid money orders may move for a consolidation order setting payments into court, which are shared equally by the creditors. While it is in force, named creditors cannot enforce except by a land writ. It ends if the debtor is 21 days in default or a new judgment is made for a later debt.

source.expect: may make a motion to the court for a consolidation order

items.title: Examination of debtor (Form 20H)
items.says: If an order is unpaid, the clerk where the debtor or other person lives or does business issues a notice of examination (Form 20H) at the creditor's request with Form 20P. The person is questioned about why they have not paid, their income, property, debts and means to pay.

source.expect: issue a notice of examination (Form 20H)

items.title: Serve the notice of examination 30 days ahead
items.says: The notice of examination, with the financial information form if applicable, is served at least 30 days before the examination date, and filed with proof of service at least three days before it.

source.expect: at least 30 days before the date fixed for the examination

review.problem: How the notice of examination is served (personally or by alternative to personal service) is in r. 8.01(10); r. 8.01(12) sets only the timing, and adds that the financial information form goes with it if applicable.

items.title: Financial information form (Form 20I)
items.says: An individual debtor being examined completes a financial information form (Form 20I), serves it on the creditor (not filed with the court), gives a copy to the judge and brings supporting documents.

source.expect: complete a financial information form (Form 20I)

items.title: Who may be examined for a business debtor
items.says: An officer or director of a corporate debtor, or the owner or a partner of a sole proprietorship or partnership, may be examined on the debtor's behalf.

source.expect: An officer or director of a corporate debtor

items.title: Examinations are private and under oath
items.says: The examination is held in private unless the court orders otherwise, under oath, and recorded.

source.expect: held in the absence of the public

items.title: Order as to payment after examination
items.says: After the examination, or on the debtor's filed consent, the court may make an order as to payment. While it is in force, named creditors may not enforce except by a land writ.

source.expect: the court may make an order as to payment

items.title: Contempt hearing
items.says: If a person served with a notice of examination does not attend, or attends but refuses to answer or produce records, the court may order them to attend a contempt hearing. The creditor serves the notice personally and files proof at least seven days before.

source.expect: fails to attend the examination

items.title: Finding of contempt for not attending
items.says: For failing to attend an examination, the court may find contempt if satisfied the person was required to attend, was properly served, did not attend, and the failure was wilful.

source.expect: the failure to attend was wilful

items.title: Setting aside an order for a contempt hearing
items.says: A person ordered to a contempt hearing for not attending may move, before the hearing date, to set the order aside; the court may instead order another examination.

source.expect: may make a motion to set aside the order

items.title: Orders at a contempt hearing (Form 20J)
items.says: At a contempt hearing, the court may order the person to attend an examination, be jailed for up to five days, attend another contempt hearing, or comply with another order. A warrant of committal (Form 20J) lasts 12 months and may be renewed.

source.expect: be jailed for a period of not more than five days

items.title: Recording that the judgment is paid
items.says: Once a judgment is paid in full, the parties may file a consent request (Form 11.2A) saying so, or the debtor may move for an order confirming full payment.

source.expect: payment has been made in full satisfaction of the order

items.title: Referees
items.says: A referee, if directed, may hear disputes about payment proposals, conduct settlement conferences, hear consolidation motions and assess disbursements. Except for terms of payment orders, a referee only reports findings to a judge.

source.expect: shall not make a final decision in any matter

items.title: Paying money into and out of court
items.says: Money in court is paid out only under a court order. The person asking for it files with the Accountant a written request for payment out with a supporting affidavit, in the Ministry's form, and a sealed copy of the order.

source.expect: Money may only be paid out of court under an order

review.problem: Rule 22.04 covers only payment out of court; the steps for paying money into court are in other parts of rule 22.

items.title: What a negligence claim must show
items.says: A person suing in negligence must show the defendant owed them a duty of care, breached the standard of care, the person suffered damage, and the damage was caused by the breach in law and in fact.

source.expect: owed him a duty of care

items.title: The but-for test for causation
items.says: Causation is generally shown by the but-for test: on a balance of probabilities, the injury would not have happened but for the defendant's negligent act.

source.expect: The test for showing causation

items.title: Shared fault reduces damages
items.says: In a negligence case, if the plaintiff's own fault contributed to the damage, the court divides the damages in proportion to each party's degree of fault.

source.expect: the court shall apportion the damages

review.problem: Equal fault where degrees cannot be determined is s. 4 of the Negligence Act, not s. 3.

items.title: Several defendants at fault
items.says: Where two or more persons are at fault, the court decides each one's degree of fault; they are jointly and severally liable to the injured person and share contribution between themselves.

source.expect: jointly and severally liable

items.title: Grant Thornton LLP v. New Brunswick (discoverability)
items.says: The Supreme Court of Canada held that a claim is discovered when the plaintiff knows, actually or constructively, the material facts from which a plausible inference of the defendant's liability can be drawn.

source.decision: Grant Thornton LLP v. New Brunswick, 2021 SCC 31
source.expect: plausible inference of liability

items.title: Mountain View Farms Ltd. v. McQueen (setting aside default judgment)
items.says: The Court of Appeal for Ontario set out the factors considered on a motion to set aside a default judgment, including how promptly the motion was brought, the explanation for the default, whether there is an arguable defence, and prejudice to each side. A

source.decision: Mountain View Farms Ltd. v. McQueen, 2014 ONCA 194
source.expect: whether the motion was brought promptly

items.title: 1196158 Ontario Inc. v. 6274013 Canada Ltd. (default judgment factors)
items.says: A Court of Appeal for Ontario decision on dismissing an action for delay at a status hearing under rule 48.14 of the Rules of Civil Procedure: the plaintiff must show an acceptable explanation for the delay and that the defendant would suffer no non-compensable prejudice. The test is conjunctive, and an unexplained delay can lead to dismissal even without proof of actual prejudice.

source.decision: 1196158 Ontario Inc. v. 6274013 Canada Ltd., 2012 ONCA 544
source.expect: The test is conjunctive, not disjunctive

review.problem: The decision is about dismissal of an action for delay at a rule 48.14 status hearing (Rules of Civil Procedure), not setting aside a default judgment.

items.title: Grover v. Hodgins (no summary judgment in Small Claims Court)
items.says: The Court of Appeal for Ontario held that the Small Claims Court has jurisdiction to award legal or equitable relief where the relief requested is a payment of money within the court's monetary limit (then $25,000) or the return of personal property valued within that limit.

source.expect: has jurisdiction to award legal or equitable relief

review.problem: The decision is about whether the Small Claims Court can grant equitable relief; it does not mention rule 12.02 or summary judgment.

items.title: Housen v. Nikolaisen (standard of review on appeal)
items.says: The Supreme Court of Canada set the standards an appeal court applies: correctness for questions of law and palpable and overriding error for findings of fact. A

source.expect: the standard of review on a question of law is that of correctness
